newsitem.title: Namibia: Namibian police clash with Bushmen over land claim.
newsitem.headline: Namibian police clash with Bushmen over land claim.

text.p: Namibian police took 70 Bushmen to court on Monday for carrying traditional weapons after a protest over land rights at the Etosha National Park.
Chief Inspector Ian Blow said the 70 were taken to two courts to be charged with possession of dangerous weapons.
He said the weapons carried by some of the demonstrators -- mostly bows and arrows but allegedly also machetes -- could have been a threat.
Up to 100 San people, widely known as Bushmen, gathered at the entrance to the park on Sunday to demand a return of their ancestral lands, now part of Namibia's foremost game reserve.
Blow said police used teargas and made the arrests after demonstrators failed to follow orders to disperse.
The demonstrators told Reuters they wanted only a place to live. "We are in a bad condition now, most are jobless, they are sleeping in the streets and just walk around," one said.

The Deputy Permanent Secretary at the Environment and Tourism Ministry, Mwanza Simenda, said on Monday that legislation was being prepared to give landless people a share in the income generated by the tourism industry.
"We recognise that there should be some kind of benefits from tourism to those communities," Simenda said.

Bushmen, renowned for their distinctive rock paintings, are among the region's earliest inhabitants. The remaining bands of Bushmen in South Africa are also trying to persuade President Nelson Mandela to give them rights to a stretch of the Kalahari Desert where their ancestors lived.
